title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
Cursor Agent, an AI assistant running Claude Sonnet, was used by Aurora ransomware operators between April and May 2026 to conduct hands-on exploitation of victim systems. The operators deployed the tool to perform network reconnaissance, credential enumeration, and lateral movement attacks across organizations. This represents a failure in access controls, where a tool designed for legitimate development assistance was used outside its intended scope to enable criminal activity.

The system lacked sufficient restrictions to prevent use for malicious purposes. An AI assistant with the capability to execute commands, install software, and interact with network infrastructure should have required stronger authentication, usage monitoring, or technical restrictions to prevent deployment by unauthorized actors. Whether such safeguards existed and failed, or were not implemented, is not established.

The incident shows that AI tools with execution capabilities can amplify the speed and scale of cybercriminal operations once obtained. What would have prevented this attack depends on factors not disclosed: whether Cursor Agent's developers knew of these risks, whether they recommended specific defensive measures to users, and whether the compromised credentials or access methods could have been detected earlier through system monitoring or threat intelligence.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group has been targeting ESXi servers since April 2026 using a Linux variant of their encryption tool. The ransomware uses ChaCha20 encryption and includes special features to target virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands. The group also deployed a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan networks for ESXi hosts and vCenter servers. Between April and May 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI assistant running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation across ten organizations, performing tasks like installing VPN clients, scanning networks, enumerating domain privileges, and attempting credential relay attacks.

Researchers also identified a second Aurora cluster operating with different techniques, affecting eight victim organizations across multiple countries including Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina. This second group used SQL Server vulnerabilities, privilege escalation tools, and S3 storage for data exfiltration. The investigation revealed multiple infrastructure indicators including command and control servers, proxy addresses, and the group's onion site used for ransom negotiations. Gambit Security published technical details and indicators of compromise to help organizations detect and defend against Aurora ransomware attacks.
